newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Albania pulls plug on Western TVs in news blackout.
newsitem.headline: Albania pulls plug on Western TVs in news blackout.

text.p: Albania pulled the plug on Western television broadcasts out of the poor Balkan country on Monday as part of a state of emergency to combat armed unrest in the south, the European Broadcasting Union said.

The Geneva-based EBU, the only organisation providing satellite television feeds to the outside world from capital Tirana, said it halted its work as of 1730 GMT after it was ordered to do so verbally by the Albanian authorities.
"We've just been told our licence is effectively suspended as a measure of the state of emergency," Tony Naetes, head of Eurovision News Services at the EBU, told Reuters.
"There was no written confirmation, it was just a verbal order from a PTT representative. This effectively prevents the most visible way of reporting the conditions in the country."

The restriction cut broadcasts by 25 Western companies and channels including Reuters Television, British Broadcasting Corporation, CNN, German networks ARD and ZDF, Italian RAI and French TFI that were being served by EBU's feed point in Tirana.

The government declared a state of emergency at the weekend and introduced a nationwide curfew and other emergency measures including media controls after two months of unrest since the collapse of dubious investment schemes climaxed this weekend.
At least 12 people were reported killed, either in clashes or by stray bullets, as demonstrators in several southern towns raided weapons depots and went on a rampage of violence.
On Monday, parliament elected President Sali Berisha, first elected in 1992, to a second five-year term in office by 113 votes in favour to one against with four abstentions.
Berisha, in a televised address on Sunday, blamed foreign intelligence services and the former communist elite for the unrest in the south.
It was not clear how the new official restrictions on the media applied to foreign news organisations and newspapers.
The International Press Institute (IPI) condemned the move to restrict press freedom and urged an end to "censorship".

"The IPI strongly condemnes the introduction by Albania's parliament of controls on the media," the Vienna-based group of editors and publishers representing media in 88 countries said in an open letter addressed to Berihsa on Monday.

"IPI believes that restrictions on the right of news media to freely gather and distribute information (are) unacceptable and urges your excellency to ensure that censorship of the media, both direct and indirect, is eliminated," it added.

Naetes said the EBU was the only organisation providing Western satellite television feed out of Albania from its mobile earth station in Tirana. The EBU had not received any orders to leave the country and was seeking clarification, he added.
